classification.difficultyReason: Select integer root candidates, test and divide successively, then factor the quadratic quotient; repeated factors use the explicitly taught procedure.

content.prompt: Factorise these polynomials into linear factors.

answer.short:
$(x+1)(x-1)(x-2)(x-3)$

Test zeros and divide successively, then factor the quadratic quotient.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}P(1)&=1-5+5+5-6\\P(1)&=0\end{align*}$$

Long division by $x-1$ gives $Q(x)=x^3-4x^2+x+6$.

$$\begin{align*}Q(-1)&=-1-4-1+6\\Q(-1)&=0\end{align*}$$

Long division of $Q(x)$ by $x+1$ gives $x^2-5x+6$.

$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x-1)(x+1)(x^2-5x+6)\\P(x)&=(x+1)(x-1)(x-2)(x-3)\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$(x+1)^2(x+5)^2$

Repeated division reveals both repeated linear factors.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}P(-1)&=1-12+46-60+25\\P(-1)&=0\end{align*}$$

Long division by $x+1$ gives $Q(x)=x^3+11x^2+35x+25$.

$$\begin{align*}Q(-1)&=-1+11-35+25\\Q(-1)&=0\end{align*}$$

Long division of $Q(x)$ by $x+1$ gives $x^2+10x+25$.

$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x+1)^2(x^2+10x+25)\\P(x)&=(x+1)^2(x+5)^2\end{align*}$$
